title: ACCESS-Style Practice Test — Form C
overview: A third full practice test in four parts: Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking. Use the strategies you practiced. Work calmly, read carefully, and do your best. The questions get a little harder as each part goes on.

sections.title: Listening
sections.directions: You will hear short talks and conversations read aloud. Listen carefully. You may hear each one one time. After listening, answer the question that follows. Choose the best answer or follow the steps in the question.

items.title: Morning Announcement
items.prompt: What time will the assembly begin?
items.correct: Correct. The speaker says the assembly begins at 10:00.
items.hint: Listen for the time that comes after the word "begin."
items.support: When a question asks "what time," listen for a clock time.
items.extension: Where will the assembly take place?

teacher.challenge: Ask for both time and place.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students point to the time.
teacher.prompt: How did you know it was 10:00?

script: Good morning, students. Today we have a special music assembly in the auditorium. Please finish your first-period work early, because the assembly will begin at ten o'clock.

items.title: Pack for the Lab
items.prompt: Which items does the teacher say to bring to the lab?
items.correct: Correct. The teacher lists a notebook, a calculator, and safety goggles.
items.hint: Track each item in the list. A soccer ball was not mentioned.
items.extension: Why would goggles be needed in a lab?

teacher.challenge: Add a distractor and ask why it does not belong.
teacher.prompt: Which item is for the math?

script: Before our lab today, make sure you bring a few things. You will need your notebook to record results, a calculator for the math, and your safety goggles.

items.title: How to Use the Microscope
items.prompt: Put the steps in the order the teacher explains for using the microscope.

items.text: Place the slide on the stage.

items.correct: Correct. Place the slide, look through the eyepiece, focus, then draw.
items.hint: Listen for first, next, then, and finally.

teacher.use: Sequencing item with academic science talk.
teacher.prompt: Which step do students skip most?

script: Here is how to use the microscope. First, place the slide on the stage. Next, look through the eyepiece. Then turn the knob to focus until the image is clear. Finally, draw what you see.

items.title: Comparing Two Cities
items.prompt: Complete the summary of what the speaker said about the two cities.

segments.text: Rivertown has 50,000 people, which makes it
than Lakeside. Of the two cities, Lakeside is the

items.correct: Correct. Rivertown is smaller than Lakeside, so Lakeside is the larger city.
items.hint: Listen for the comparison words and the population numbers.
items.extension: How many more people live in Lakeside?

teacher.use: Harder item combining data and comparison.
teacher.lower: Show the two numbers written down.
teacher.challenge: Add a third city and ask which is largest.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students fill a printed summary.
teacher.prompt: How do you know which city is larger?

script: Let's compare two cities in our state. Rivertown has fifty thousand people. Lakeside has eighty thousand people, so Rivertown is smaller than Lakeside. Now complete the summary.

sections.title: Reading
sections.directions: Read each passage carefully. Then answer the question or follow the steps. You may read each passage again. Choose the best answer or click the correct part of the text.

items.title: Finding a Detail
items.prompt: Click the sentence that tells WHY the desert fox has large ears.
passage: The fennec fox lives in the hot, sandy desert.
It is small, with soft fur the color of sand.
Its very large ears help the fox release heat and stay cool.
At night, the fox hunts for insects and small animals.

sentences.text: The fennec fox lives in the hot, sandy desert.
It is small, with soft fur the color of sand.
Its very large ears help the fox release heat and stay cool.
At night, the fox hunts for insects and small animals.

items.correct: Correct. The large ears help the fox release heat and stay cool.
items.hint: The question asks "why." Find the sentence about the ears.
items.support: Scan for the key word "ears" and look for a reason.
items.extension: What does the fox eat at night?
readFor: what helps the fox stay cool

teacher.challenge: Find the detail and one more fact.
teacher.prompt: Why are big ears useful in a desert?

items.title: Main Idea
items.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: The fennec fox lives in the hot, sandy desert.
It is small, with soft fur the color of sand.
Its very large ears help the fox release heat and stay cool.
At night, the fox hunts for insects and small animals.

options.text: The fennec fox has features that help it live in the desert.
The fennec fox has soft fur.
The fennec fox hunts at night.

items.correct: Correct. The main idea covers all the features that help the fox live in the desert.
items.hint: The main idea covers the whole passage, not one feature.
items.support: Choices b and c are details. The main idea ties them together.
items.extension: Write a title that matches the main idea.
readFor: an idea bigger than a detail

teacher.lower: Ask if each choice covers everything.
teacher.challenge: Students justify why details are too narrow.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students point to the broadest choice.
teacher.prompt: How is the main idea bigger than a detail?

items.title: Two Reasons
items.prompt: Which TWO reasons does the writer give for joining the school garden club?
passage: Our school garden club meets every Tuesday after school.
Members learn how to grow vegetables and care for plants.
You also make new friends while you work together.
The club meets in the courtyard near the cafeteria.

options.text: You learn to grow vegetables and care for plants.
The club meets near the cafeteria.

items.correct: Correct. The two reasons are learning to grow plants and making new friends.
items.hint: A reason tells WHY to join. Two choices are just facts about when and where.
items.extension: Which detail tells WHERE the club meets?

teacher.lower: Read each option and ask: is it a reason or a fact?
teacher.challenge: Add a third reason as a distractor.
teacher.noTech: Print; students check the two reasons.
teacher.prompt: How is a reason different from a fact about time?

items.title: Word in Context
items.prompt: Complete the sentence about what the underlined word means.
passage: The soil in our garden was dry and hard at first.
We added water and compost until it became rich and easy to dig.

segments.text: In the passage, the word "soil" means the

items.correct: Correct. "Soil" is the dirt plants grow in, and "rich" here means full of nutrients.
items.hint: Use the nearby words: dig, water, and compost.
items.support: Context clues are the words around an unknown word.
items.extension: Use the word "soil" in your own sentence.

teacher.prompt: Which words helped you define rich?

sections.title: Writing
sections.directions: Read each task carefully. Plan your ideas, then write a clear response in complete sentences. Use the word bank and sentence frames to help you. Take your time and check your work.

items.title: Explain a Process
items.prompt: Explain how to study for a test. Write 4-6 sentences using order words.
items.correct: Good work. A strong response uses order words and clear, complete sentences.
items.hint: Use a different order word for each step and tell why it helps.
items.support: Structure: first, next, then, finally. Begin each sentence with an order word.
items.extension: Add one sentence about what to do the night before the test.

teacher.lower: Provide a frame for each step.
teacher.prompt: Why does order matter when you explain a process?

items.title: State and Support an Opinion
items.prompt: Some schools want to give every student a tablet for class. Do you agree or disagree? Write a paragraph that states your opinion and gives two reasons.
items.correct: Good work. A strong response states a clear opinion and supports it with reasons and a conclusion.
items.hint: Start with your opinion, give two reasons with examples, and end with a conclusion.
items.support: Structure: claim, reason one, reason two, conclusion. Use transitions to connect ideas.
items.extension: Add a sentence that responds to someone who disagrees.

teacher.function: Writing a claim with supporting reasons.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.directions: You will be given a topic and a short time to plan. Then you will speak your answer aloud in complete sentences. Use the sentence frames to organize your ideas. Speak clearly and stay on the topic.

items.title: Describe and Explain
items.prompt: Describe a hobby you enjoy and explain why you like it. Speak 4-5 sentences.
items.correct: Good work. A strong answer describes the hobby and gives clear reasons.
items.hint: Name the hobby, describe it, and use "because" to explain why you like it.
items.support: Use the frame "My favorite hobby is ___ because ___."
items.extension: Compare it to another hobby you like less.
items.adminScript: Think about a hobby you enjoy. I want you to describe it and explain why you like it. Speak four or five sentences. You have one minute to plan, then you will speak.

teacher.prompt: What made that your favorite hobby?

items.title: Give an Opinion with Reasons
items.prompt: Should students be allowed to use phones during lunch? Give your opinion and support it with two reasons. Speak 5-6 sentences.
items.correct: Good work. A strong answer states an opinion and supports it with two clear reasons.
items.hint: State your opinion, give two reasons with "because," and end with a conclusion.
items.support: Structure: opinion, reason one, reason two, conclusion.
items.extension: Mention a reason someone might disagree, then respond.
items.adminScript: Think about whether students should be allowed to use phones during lunch. I want your opinion. Speak five or six sentences. State your opinion and give two reasons using the word because. Finish with a conclusion. You have two minutes to plan, then you will speak.

teacher.use: Final speaking task, opinion with support.
teacher.function: Stating and defending an opinion orally.
